brief: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigned; interim CEO Colette Kress had already cut Nvidia's OpenAI backstop in half, putting cautious management over the AI trade's main financier, a $99bn equity book plus $530.5bn of commitments. Goldman's Schneider expects signed commitments honored but new rounds harder, and UBS's Arcuri says a Nvidia pause could pull roughly $50bn out of the system. AI high-yield spreads have widened to about 425bp versus 265bp for non-AI BB/B paper, with no new AI junk deals since September, Goldman's Wheeler says, because investment-grade tenant wraps only activate once a building is complete. Goldman's 2027 outlook forecasts S&P earnings growth falling from 36% this year to 11% in 2027 as hyperscaler capex's EPS contribution fades from 12pp to 9pp, then flips to a 5pp drag by 2028 as depreciation rises. AI capex is projected to reach $1.4 trillion annualized, 4% of GDP, by end-2027 while adding only 0.2pp to GDP growth, since imported chips subtract from GDP. Hot CPI and PPI prints, a floated 50bp December hike and weak Treasury auctions show the Fed no longer looking through inflation; stocks rallied anyway because forced sellers had already de-grossed, leaving positioning as a tailwind against a Fed-driven headwind.
